text:
I


To Cuernavaca I go, sweet retreat,

when, through whim or discouragement,

I yield to the desire to interrupt the tale

and give my story some breathing room.


To Cuernavaca I go, asking only

to enjoy its airs for a moment:

a pause of freedom and recreation

a sigh's brief distance away.


Neither country nor city, summit nor hollow;

beatific solitude, quiet that soothes,

or gentle company without surfeit.


Vegetal warmth in which being rocks

in philosophical measure...

To Cuernavaca I go, to Cuernavaca!


II


I do not know whether I inspire it with my mood

or whether repose is granted me by design.

Whether reality or pretense,

why do I ask myself, why do I rave?


It is enough for me to know, sweet retreat,

that you soothe my temples with your breath:

a pause of freedom and recreation

a sigh's brief distance away.


The quiet and the light the soul drinks

like cordial wine; the magpie trills,

and the laurel murmurs of birds;


a cloud flies; a star stands out,

and time itself suspends and lasts...

To Cuernavaca I go, to Cuernavaca!

translation.title: To Cuernavaca!
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated destination refrain and the poem’s balanced contrast between retreat, freedom, quiet, and light.
